analysis.title: Kosmos Energy Ltd. (KOS): First Take: EBITDA Miss; Focus on Balance Sheet Management, Gulf Outlook, and Tortue Phase 1+ Progress
key_insights: KOS reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $0.06 vs. GS estimate of $0.18 and FactSet consensus of $0.09. Adjusted EBITDA was $283.3mn vs. GS estimate of $343.4mn, a $60.1mn shortfall.

4Q26 production guidance is 60-64 MBOE/d vs. GS published estimate of ~75 MBOE/d. Management expects lower Gulf of America output next quarter from planned maintenance, workovers and storm disruptions.

Volume and price both missed GS estimates. Net liquids sold were 3,786 MBbls vs. 4,613 MBbls estimated. Unhedged realized oil price was $88.57/bbl vs. $98.67/bbl estimated, and hedged was $81.64/bbl vs. $89.03/bbl.
Ghana: production averaged ~40.5 kboe/d net in 3Q, Jubilee averaged ~84.5 kboe/d gross, TEN averaged ~14.6 kboe/d gross, and the company reported 2.75 Jubilee cargo liftings.
Jubilee: the 2025/26 drilling campaign finished with seven successful infill wells. In September the partnership secured a rig for the 2027/28 program of up to 10 wells, starting mid-2027.
Gulf of America production averaged ~14.1 kboe/d net in 3Q. GTA Phase 1 averaged ~14.6 kboe/d net, with ~8.5 gross LNG cargoes lifted.

Balance sheet: the RBL facility amendment and extension is complete, and the company remains on track for a 20% reduction in net debt this year. GS asks whether 2028 maturities can be addressed later this year.

GS conference call questions cover uses of cash and remaining maturities, Jubilee production when the next campaign starts in mid-2027, Gulf of America output and Trailblazer drilling, the SHEL exploration alliance, the Tiberius farm-down's effect on near-term cash flow, Tortue Phase 1+ cost reduction, and capital spend and costs for next year.

GS keeps a Sell rating on KOS with a 6-month DCF/M&A-based price target of $2.75 vs. a $2.85 price (30 Oct close), implying 3.5% downside. Key risks are commodity prices, capital spend and operational execution.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Sell after a 3Q26 EBITDA and EPS miss and 4Q26 production guidance well below its estimate. The 6-month DCF/M&A-based target of $2.75 sits 3.5% below the $2.85 price.
